Q: Selenium ChromeDriver randomly crashes with 'chrome not reachable' error even in headless mode A:

Chrome v120 & ChromeDriver v120 is old and outdated. Accordingly the failure reasons can be numerous. Additionally you haven't mentioned the Selenium version you are using.

Solution

Ensure the following:

  • Chrome Browser is updated to current chrome=143.0
  • Selenium is upgraded to current released Version 4.39.0 and let the in-built Selenium Manager download the matching ChromeDriver for the program execution.

Your minimal code block can be:

from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options

options = Options()
options.add_argument("--headless")
options.add_argument("--screen-info={0,0 1920x1080}")

driver = webdriver.Chrome(options=options)
try:
    driver.get("https://example.com")
    print(driver.title)
finally:
    driver.quit()

tl; dr

Note:

  • With Chrome in headless mode --window-size=1920,1080 no longer works and you need to use --screen-info={0,0 1920x1080}
  • Avoid using the options --no-sandbox, --disable-dev-shm-usage, --disable-gpu, etc unless they are absolutely necessary.

Q: JSON response difference in Spring Boot v3 and v4 A:

spring.jackson.use-jackson2-defaults=true should help

If you prefer at least initially keep using default settings as close as possible as Jackson 2, you can use the spring.jackson.use-jackson2-defaults property. When set to true, the auto-configured JsonMapper will have defaults that align as closely as possible with those of Jackson 2 in Spring Boot 3. https://spring.io/blog/2025/10/07/introducing-jackson-3-support-in-spring

Q: Is kill function synchronous? A:

kill is sometimes synchronous (*).

For a program that

  • is single-threaded (**),
  • does not block the signal,
  • tries to kill itself,
  • has no other pending unblocked signal,

then it is "synchronous".

(*): in the sense that the signal will be delivered before the kill() function call returns.

(**): technically if the program is multithreaded, but all other threads block the signal, the behavior is also satisfied. The condition listed above is sufficient, but not necessary.

From POSIX specification:

If the value of pid causes sig to be generated for the sending process, and if sig is not blocked for the calling thread and if no other thread has sig unblocked or is waiting in a sigwait() function for sig, either sig or at least one pending unblocked signal shall be delivered to the sending thread before kill() returns.

Credit: https://stackoverflow.com/a/54624877/5267751

Q: polar plot -- sin transformation A:

ideally as a sin wave along a circular path

It already is that.

this has a bug that is, it compresses as r getting lower and expands when r getting higher

It might be visually unintended, but keep in mind that any 'decompression' you perform will produce a function that is not a sine wave, but some other periodic function. You say that your plot "does not preserve the angles of a [sine] wave", and well... it's impossible to preserve the angles of a sine wave after a polar projection.

If you're making this for some decorative or visual purpose, that's not well-defined, but we can guess at some characteristics of a new function:

  • Don't transform b + a*cos(nt); instead add some transformation f as b + a*cos(f(nt))
  • f must intersect x=x at every multiple of pi radians
  • f < x iff 0 < x < pi
  • f > x iff pi < x < 2pi

Any function you can come up with that satisfies those criteria will have the decompression effect that you describe. Here is a very simple one:

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def flower(
    n_petals: int, amplitude: float, base_radius: float, n_theta: int = 501,
    antidistortion: float = 0.5,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    theta = np.linspace(start=-np.pi, stop=+np.pi, num=n_theta)
    wt = n_petals*theta
    # wt must be invariant at 0, pi, 2pi
    wt += antidistortion*np.sin(wt)
    radius = base_radius + amplitude*np.cos(wt)
    return theta, radius


def main() -> None:
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(subplot_kw={'projection': 'polar'})
    ax.plot(*flower(n_petals=5, amplitude=2, base_radius=5, antidistortion=0),
        label='a=0', alpha=0.3)
    ax.plot(*flower(n_petals=5, amplitude=2, base_radius=5),
        label='a=0.5')
    ax.legend()
    ax.grid(True)
    plt.show()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

Q: Selenium/Python: Trying to display choices in a dropdown menu A:

As per the given HTML the <ul> tag is having multiple class values:

<ul class="SLP-dropdown-menu SLP-dropdown-menu-root SLP-dropdown-menu-vertical" role-“menu" tabindex="0">

So using a single class value i.e. SLP-dropdown-menu within the xpath:

//ul[@class='SLP-dropdown-menu']

won't be sufficient to locate the desired element. Hence the line of code:

driver.find_element(By.XPATH, "//ul[@class='SLP-dropdown-menu']")

fails with the error NoSuchElementException

Solution

To locate and click on the desired <ul> element you can use either of the following locator strategies:

  • Using XPATH:

    driver.find_element(By.XPATH, "//ul[@class='SLP-dropdown-menu SLP-dropdown-menu-root SLP-dropdown-menu-vertical']").click()

  • Using CSS_SELECTOR:

    driver.find_element(By.CSS_SELECTOR, "ul.SLP-dropdown-menu.SLP-dropdown-menu-root.SLP-dropdown-menu-vertical").click()

Ideally, to locate the clickable element you should remove all the instances of implicitly_wait(n) with WebDriverWait for the element_to_be_clickable() and you can use either of the following locator strategies:

  • Using XPATH:

     WebDriverWait(driver, 20).until(EC.element_to_be_clickable((By.XPATH, "//ul[@class='SLP-dropdown-menu SLP-dropdown-menu-root SLP-dropdown-menu-vertical']"))).click()

  • Using CSS_SELECTOR:

    WebDriverWait(driver, 20).until(EC.element_to_be_clickable((By.CSS_SELECTOR, "ul.SLP-dropdown-menu.SLP-dropdown-menu-root.SLP-dropdown-menu-vertical"))).click()

  • Note : You have to add the following imports :

    from selenium.webdriver.support.ui import WebDriverWait
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By
from selenium.webdriver.support import expected_conditions as EC

Q: Airflow 3.0.2 LDAP / Active Directory Authentication Not Working with FabAuthManager A:

In Airflow 3, new configurations are added to the apiserver instead of the webserver.

For Example:

LDAP configurations can be set up this way.

apiServer:
  apiServerConfig: | 

    from __future__ import annotations

    import os

    from flask_appbuilder.const import AUTH_LDAP

    basedir = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname(__file__))

Q: In terminal (Bash), how do you autocomplete partial matches in the middle of a filename? A:

A little late, but in bash the closest to completion with partial match (present in zsh) I got, is using fzf double asterisk completion:

vim h**<TAB>

Personally, I don't like to double tap any key, so I changed fzf's configuration to only one:

# On .bashrc: export FZF_COMPLETION_TRIGGER='*'
vim h*<TAB>
